item.title: Partnerships and Fundraising Manager
item.description: Partnerships and Fundraising Manager AGE Platform Europe Brussels, Belgium € 2000 - € 2500 per month gross Location: Brussels, Belgium (*), or remote work with periodic visits to headquarters in Brussels Working hours: Part-time (+/-10 days per month) Reporting to: Secretary General Contract type: Employee contract in Belgium, one-year with possibility of extension to unlimited contract; or Self-employed consultant contract, one-year with possibility of extension. Monthly gross salary: Employee contract: range of 2000-2200 EUR depending on candidate’s profile and experience; or Self-employed consultancy: max. €2500 VAT excl. (*) If you are not an EU citizen, please indicate whether you currently hold a work permit for Belgium. Background AGE Platform Europe (AGE) brings together over one hundred organisations of and working for older people, with a mission to enable everyone to live a full and dignified life based on human rights and age equality throughout the life. To that end, we empower older people to get involved in debates on ageing and to impact policy making toward inclusive societies for all ages: “We are the experts of our own lives. Our community is extremely diverse, but our difference is our strength when we speak together. As self-advocates, we have the potential to contribute expertise, skills and experience that enrich our societies and make them more just, inclusive and prosperous.” To know more about our vision, mission, core values and principles, and advocacy goals, see AGE's Strategy 2026-2030 ‘Towards a Society for All Ages’ . Purpose of role AGE is seeking a proactive and self-driven Partnerships and Fundraising Manager to identify and build the right partnerships to raise money which will help AGE to advance its mission. You will expand our reach, enhance fundraising efforts and, eventually, create lasting impact for age equality in old age. We are looking for a person with proven experience and tenacity, recognising that securing funds for the cause of age equality and the human rights of older people requires sustained effort and a creative approach. Whether integrated into the AGE staff in Brussels or as a self-employed independent consultant, you will play a crucial role in diversifying our revenue streams. This effort is part of an initiative to reinforce external fundraising, supplementing contributions from AGE members and institutional grants. With firsthand experience in managing an innovative fundraising environment, your passion and drive to make a difference and achieve results are crucial. These qualities will help progress towards the AGE's vision of a Society for All Ages . Primary responsibilities As Partnerships and Fundraising Manager, you will be expected to uphold the organisation’s vision and core values, as set out in its 2026–2030 strategy. This is a hands-on position and highly demanding role, in which will have the following key responsibilities: Implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy, actively seek out new funding opportunities, and cultivate relationships with private donors; Support the development and oversee the delivery of diverse partnerships and fundraising portfolio tailored to the needs of our network of organizations serving older people; Involve co-creating, building upon the current fundraising strategy, planning, executing, and monitoring partnerships and fundraising activities; Collaborate directly with the Secretary General and the Finance Manager and, as the partnerships/fundraising portfolio is extensive and varied, you will also work with the Policy and Communications teams. Your qualifications Essential At least five years of professional experience in fundraising development and tools such as pitches, proposals, due diligence, pipeline mapping etc., preferably within the non-profit sector; Commitment to the cause of human rights in general, and to age equality throughout life in particular; Minimum knowledge of EU social policies including human rights aspects; Have a pragmatic, creative and innovative approach to problem solving and decision making; Excellent time management and organisation skills, to be able to manage multiple tasks at once; Proficiency in English (writing and speaking) and excellent communication skills to communicate and build relationships with an array of people; Strong networking and relationship-building abilities; Enthusiastic and proactive, with perseverance and a can-do attitude; Enjoy collaborating with other team members. Desirable Previous experience in NGO sector and in the fields of social/ageing/human rights policies; Some experience in budget setting and management; Experienced in IT - using databases to log and keep information accurately up to date, in a timely manner; Some knowledge of French. How to apply for the post Please submit to maciej.kucharczyk@age-platform.eu : a copy of your CV/resume, and a cover letter (maximum 300 words) outlining your interest in age equality throughout life and in the role and how you fulfil the requirements set out in this job announcement. Only candidates shortlisted for interviews will be contacted. The deadline for application: Sunday 16 August, 23:59 CEST (Brussels time) Interviews (two rounds): Will take place online: first, in late September and, second, in October Starting date: Ideally 1 November 2026 AGE is an equal opportunity employer. We actively promote equality, diversity and inclusion. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.title: Senior Researcher ‘Just Transition/Foresight’ (m/f/x)
item.description: Senior Researcher ‘Just Transition/Foresight’ (m/f/x) ETUI - European Trade Union Institute Brussels, Belgium From € 6195 per month gross Status: Full-time – Permanent Department: Foresight Unit Application Deadline: 1 st September 2026 Estimated starting date: January 2027 ABOUT THE ETUI The ETUI provides research and training support to the European trade union movement. The Brussels-based Institute conducts research into European issues of strategic importance for the world of labour and promotes education and training activities with the aim of enhancing the capacity of workers’ organisations to contribute to social dialogue and building a social Europe. ABOUT THE POSITION The ETUI is seeking a senior researcher, ideally with team-leading experience, to join our staff. Working within a dynamic, international environment, you will be responsible for conducting research into future-oriented topics of relevance for the world of work, in particular Just Transition. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Conducting own empirical research into future-oriented topics of relevance for the European trade unions and policymakers, in particular Just Transition and the economic, employment and social implications of structural transformations, be they technology or policy-driven; Communicating research findings to diverse audiences (academia, trade unions, policymakers, media); Contribute to the conception and coordination of the ETUI’s work programme in the area of foresight/just transition and monitor progress of the work programme in this area. QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS REQUIRED A PhD in a relevant social science discipline (economics, political economy, sociology, political science); Strong quantitative skills; Familiarity with foresight and scenario-building methodologies; Proven research excellence; Ability to communicate complex material to different audiences; Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work in a multilingual and multicultural environment. KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE At least 7 years’ relevant experience; experience in a non-profit or international organisation with a research focus is an asset; Proficiency in relevant econometric/data software and standard ICT tools (MS Office 365, including SharePoint and Teams); Project-management experience is essential and team-leading experience an asset; Excellent command of English; French and other languages are a significant asset; Knowledge of European Union institutions and of the trade union movement is a distinct advantage; Experience of working in a politically sensitive environment is an advantage. CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT The ETUI offers a challenging role in a dynamic environment that bridges academic research and European policymaking. We provide a competitive salary and an attractive benefits package in line with qualifications and experience. The ETUI is an equal opportunities employer. Starting salary for Category A2 is €6195 gross per month (based on full-time employment). In accordance with the ETUI’s internal policy, this role allows for a maximum of 10 days of remote work per month (pro-rata for part-time staff). HOW TO APPLY Please address your application (CV, motivation letter, supporting documents) to Andrew Watt, General director at vacancy@etui.org by 1 September 2026 . We appreciate the interest of all applicants; however, please note that only shortlisted candidates will be formally contacted to proceed to the next stage (written assignment and panel interview in September 2026). We thank you for your understanding and for your interest in the ETUI. GDPR: The ETUI processes your personal data for recruitment purposes in accordance with our Internal Recruitment Policy. Your application files will be retained for a maximum of 3 months following the conclusion of the recruitment process, after which they will be permanently deleted. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.description: Expression of Interest (EOI) - Roster of Individual Consultants for International IDEA's Ukraine Democracy-Assistance Portfolio International IDEA - The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance Reference No: 2026-06-094 Deadline for Submissions: Proposals must be submitted on or before 23:59 (CET), 21 August, 2026 . Late submissions will not be considered for evaluation. Address for Submissions: E-mail: ukraine.roster@idea.int This email address is set up with auto-response to acknowledge emails received. In the event that you did not receive an autoreply, please send a text message prior to the deadline for submission (NO CALLS, CALLS WILL NOT BE ANSWERED) to this number +46725375735 prior to the deadline for submission . In your text message, please provide the following: EOI reference no. and title; Email address you used for submission; Date and Time, you sent your submission (e.g. 01 December 2021, 12:30 CET ); The above information must also be sent to eoi@idea.int before the deadline for submission. Format for Submissions: Applicants are requested to submit their application by email, following the submission requirements set out in Section 2 of the EOI. Email subject line: Use the format "EOI 2026-06-094 – [Your Full Name]" . Example: EOI 2026-06-094 – John Smith Email Address for Clarifications: eoi@idea.int Clarifications may be requested via e-mail no later than 7 August prior to the submission deadline at the above email address. Note a response to a request for clarifications will be issued on our website http://www.idea.int/ . Therefore, please check the website regularly during the process. Important Note: there are two different email addresses as outlined above, one to be used for Submission of your final proposal and the second one to be used for clarifications and other related correspondence. Section 1. Background About International IDEA The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA) is an intergovernmental organization with a mission to advance democracy worldwide as a universal human aspiration and an enabler of sustainable development. We do this by shaping, strengthening, and safeguarding democratic political institutions and processes at all levels. About the Ukraine Democracy-Assistance Portfolio International IDEA implements a democracy-assistance portfolio in Ukraine focused on supporting the country's democratic institutions and electoral processes in a particularly demanding context. The portfolio covers a broad range of workstreams, including electoral assistance, electoral risk management, strategic communications, gender mainstreaming, political finance, parliamentary strengthening, constitutional building, EU integration, political party assistance, countering disinformation, FIMI, ICT and cybersecurity for electoral management bodies, social media monitoring, and capacity building through the Central Election Commission's Training Centre. To support the effective implementation of this portfolio, International IDEA seeks to establish a roster of qualified individual consultants – both international and national - with subject matter expertise across these workstreams. We now seek expressions of interest from qualified individuals to add to a roster of consultants from which we may call off services as required. Inclusion in the roster is not a guarantee that you will be contracted for any work. Each piece of work will have terms of reference drafted which will include expected deliverables and an anticipated timeframe for delivery. If your skills match the requirements, you will then be requested to confirm your availability and provide a quotation for the work required. Several consultants may be approached to provide quotations for each piece of work. If agreement is reached, a contract will be entered into for that work. Inclusion in the roster does not constitute a guarantee of any contract with International IDEA. When a consultant is selected for a specific assignment, a Supply Contract will be issued in line with International IDEA's procurement policies and procedures. Please note that if you respond to this EOI we will include your CV in a roster that may be accessed by Staff Members for the purposes of determining your suitability to be approached for specific assignments. Please see our Privacy Policy ( Privacy Policy | International IDEA ) to understand how we treat your personal data. Consultants accepted into the roster will be retained for a period of five (5) years from the date of the EOI award. International IDEA reserves the right to extend the validity period of the roster as needed. If your contact details or other relevant information change during the validity of the roster, or if you wish to withdraw your application or be removed from the roster at any time, please notify International IDEA by email at consultants.roster@idea.int . Section 2. Requirements Applicants interested in being included in the roster are requested to submit the documents listed below as part of their application. Please ensure that the documents are arranged in the order listed below. 2.1 A cover letter with your motivation for applying to be part of the roster. 2.2 A CV in English which clearly outlines how your details match the requirements and including: Your experience with relevant dates; Your educational qualifications; and The names and contact details of at least two references. 2.3 A completed Roster Questionnaire (Annex A). The Roster Questionnaire includes information on your thematic areas of expertise, regional experience, years of experience, language proficiency (English, Ukrainian, and other languages), proposed daily rate in EUR, and bank information for future payment purposes. 2.4 A Declaration of Honour form signed. A completed and signed declaration of honour form. For Section VI – Declaration on honour on restrictive measures: Please tick “YES” to confirm that the candidate/tenderer is not subject to any restrictive measures or sanctions as described in this section. Section 3. Criteria 3.1 Applications will be reviewed based on the documentation submitted. Inclusion in the roster will be based on the following criteria: Relevant professional experience in the thematic area(s) selected; Academic qualifications and professional certifications; Regional expertise, particularly in Ukraine or similar contexts; Language proficiency in English and Ukrainian; Proposed daily rate in EUR, considered in relation to the level of expertise and in line with International IDEA's policies for individual consultants. 3.2 Applicants may apply to multiple thematic areas in a single submission. Section 4. Final Considerations 4.1 International IDEA will not be bound to select any of the consultants or firms that apply and reserves the right to cancel this EOI at any stage of the process without any obligation to applicants. 4.2 The following documents are enclosed with this EOI Cover Page: Annex A – Roster Questionnaire; Annex B – Declaration of Honour Form; General Terms and Conditions. 4.3 Complaints regarding any aspect of the EOI process should be addressed in writing to both the Internal Auditor and the Executive Director at International IDEA. The address is tender.complaints@idea.int . The Expression of Interest Notice, Roster Questionnaire, Declaration of Honour Form and General Terms and Conditions are available at: https://www.idea.int/about-us/procurement-and-tenders . Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.description: Public Affairs Intern ISDI - International Special Dietary Foods Industries Brussels, Belgium About ISDI: ISDI is the leading international expert association on special dietary foods. It brings together national and international associations active in this food sector from more than 20 countries on over 6 continents. ISDI is an industry platform for debate on regulatory, technical and scientific issues regarding special dietary foods. Position overview: We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Public Affairs Intern to join our team. This role presents a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of public health and food science and nutrition. The intern will provide essential support for ongoing initiatives in the field of special dietary foods (including infant and young child nutrition policy at international level) and support advocacy efforts by ISDI members. Key responsibilities: Support and monitoring on policy developments: Conduct monitoring with a focus on the UN system related to infant & young child nutrition, summarise key updates; Writing: Support the development of materials, including data trends and analysis for stakeholder engagement and advocacy; Stakeholder engagement: Collaborate with internal teams, external consultants and member organisations to support projects and initiatives and prepare advocacy efforts; Support for experts and team: Active support with preparing materials for internal and external sector-specific meetings, and providing other operational support as needed. Qualifications: A self-starter who can navigate complex issues and environments; Education: Recent graduate or nearing the completion of a degree in political science, public health, law, international relations or food and nutrition; Research skills: Strong research, analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to synthesise complex information; Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English with an emphasis on writing but also on articulating messages to different audiences. Other UN languages are a plus. What we offer: You will work within the ISDI team, composed of the Secretary-General, Communications Manager and Scientific & Regulatory Affairs Officer. You will also work closely with the chairs of our Public Policy Working Group and experts from within the ISDI membership. Benefits of the internship: Gain hands-on experience in public affairs, food and nutrition policies and industry advocacy; Work alongside industry experts and expand your professional network; Build technical skills in policy research, technical writing and data analysis. How to apply: We encourage young professionals from all regions of the world to apply. The successful candidate can work out of our office in Brussels, but remote work is possible for the right candidate. Please note that we are not able to sponsor a work permit for Belgium. Ideal candidates should submit the following materials using the Apply Now button below: CV; Cover letter outlining interest in the role and relevant experience; Writing sample (e.g., research paper or policy document) that demonstrates analytical and writing skills. Apply Now Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.title: Project & Administrative Assistant (Intern: CIP)
item.description: Project & Administrative Assistant (Intern: CIP) EATG - European AIDS Treatment Group Brussels, Belgium € 1,300 per month gross Contract Type: 1-year contract (Convention d’Immersion Professionnelle (CIP)) Working Time: 38 hours per week with flexible working hours About EATG The European AIDS Treatment Group (EATG) is a patient-led NGO that advocates for excellent care, treatment, and prevention of HIV and related infections. We fight for equitable access to healthcare for all affected communities across Europe. The internship Are you passionate about social justice, global health, science and community advocacy? We are looking for a motivated intern to join us for a structured, 12-month professional immersion plan. You will progressively learn how to support HIV-related projects, community engagement activities, and NGO administrative workflows. Who You Are (Requirements) Your Values & Mindset Mission-Driven: A strong interest and commitment to supporting people living with HIV and communities disproportionately affected or at risk; Interpersonal Skills: An open-minded, non-discriminatory, and collaborative team player who handles confidential information with discretion; Work Style: Organised, proactive, and comfortable working with increasing autonomy. Your Skills & Background Education & Experience: Relevant academic background or equivalent work experience. Previous experience in the NGO sector is considered an asset. An academic focus on Gender Studies, Diversity & Inclusion, Social Science, Human Rights, Medical Science or Public Health is a strong advantage; Communication: Excellent command of written and spoken English with strong writing skills. Any additional language is an asset. Excellent command of creating and critically evaluating AI-generated content , with strong analytical and editorial expertise; Technical: Prior experience in supporting project coordination and administration, social media management, or using CMS/website tools is a plus. Logistics & Eligibility Right to Work: You must hold EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship, a valid Belgian residence permit, or a visa that legally allows you to undertake a training contract in Belgium; Relocation: Ability to move to Belgium in time for the start of the internship; Travel: Willingness and availability to travel if required. What You Will Learn & Do Over 12 months, your responsibilities and autonomy will grow through a structured learning plan, including the following Months 1–4 (Foundations & Autonomy): Learn the basics of HIV advocacy, support project coordination, handle basic admin tasks, learn internal tools, shadow managers, begin drafting documentation, monitor and report on upcoming key events and fundraising opportunities as well as support community engagement and conduct desk research; M onths 5–8 (Project Support & Coordination): Help coordinate event logistics, draft social media and newsletter content, manage segments of ongoing projects and activities. Report on events/activities and produce communication materials; Months 9–12 (Advanced Coordination & Growth): Manage full workflows independently, prepare detailed project documentation, support monitoring and evaluation activities, take full ownership of coordinating a small project or project segment with limited supervision, and engage in career planning. What We Offer Financial Package: €1,300 gross per month plus 100% public transport subscription (home - office) ; Professional Growth: Direct European NGO experience, an Individual Development Plan (IDP), dedicated training budget, and the opportunity to develop skills in health, human rights advocacy, community engagement processes, research, and communication, with regular supervision; Time Off: 10 days of paid holiday; Flexible Working & Work from Abroad: Work from home options included. After successful onboarding and confirmation, you can request short-term remote work blocks from international locations , subject to management approval; Work Environment: A friendly, collegial team in a modern coworking space next to Metro Trône, Brussels (including free coffee/tea, communal garden, kitchen, and cafeteria). How to Apply Please apply to application@eatg.org , attaching one pdf file containing only a cover letter (maximum 1 page) and a CV (maximum 2 pages), in English, detailing your competencies, experience and motivation relevant to this role and your reasons for applying for the post. The file name and the email subject must include the job title and your full name. Deadline for application: 31 st August 2026 Tentative dates for online interviews: 15 th and 16 th September 2026 Our policy on the use of AI All submitted applications should be original and drafted by the applicant. We strongly encourage you to draft your cover letter and show us your writing, problem-solving, and experience. We are interested in learning more about you, your background and your motivation for the role. AI tools may be used for spelling, formatting, and grammar, but text generated by AI must not be submitted. We expect a high number of applications to be received, and it is clear when applications have been written by AI, as they tend to look similar. These applications are difficult to assess and are rated poorly as a result. We kindly ask that you disclose how you used AI when sending your CV and cover letter. Any application arriving after the deadline or without the stipulated file requirements will not be considered. The EATG is an “equal opportunity employer” with a focus on the GIPA/MIPA principle. The employer will not discriminate and will take “affirmative action” measures to ensure against discrimination in employment, recruitment, advertisements for employment, compensation, termination, upgrading, promotions, and other conditions of employment against any employee or job applicant on the bases of race, creed, colour, age, national origin, sex and gender identity, expression and orientation, disability, and health status. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.title: Fundraising and Development Officer
item.description: Fundraising and Development Officer EEB - European Environmental Bureau Brussels, Belgium From € 3101 per month gross Come join Europe’s largest network of environmental citizens’ organisations and contribute to strategic fundraising for a resilient, mobilised and vibrant civil society and a better future where people and nature thrive together. About us The EEB is the largest network of environmental citizens’ organisations in Europe . We bring together over 190 member organisations from more than 40 countries, representing some 30 million individual members and supporters. We advocate for progressive policies to create a better future where people and nature thrive together . Our commitment to fairness, equality, diversity and wellbeing The EEB strives to be a fair, inclusive, safe place and a welcoming and learning organisation. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates. Your experience matters . Please consult our Diversity, Equality and Inclusion Policy . Please do not use pictures in your CV. Do leave out any information that may contribute to unconscious bias such as reference to your nationality, date or place of birth. We respect our employees’ lives outside of work, support colleagues in care roles, and take work-life balance and wellbeing seriously. How You Will Have an Impact As our next Fundraising and Development Officer, you will be at the heart of the implementation of the EEB’s fundraising strategy supporting donor relations, directly initiating and managing applications and coordinating fundraising efforts across our teams. This is an exciting role for someone with an entrepreneurial mindset. You will join one of Europe’s leading environmental NGOs on its journey to secure and diversify its funding streams at a pivotal moment of time leading up to the 2029 European elections and beyond . In your role, you will support the Senior Management Team and internal Fundraising Team with the implementation of action plans in line with our Fundraising Strategy, engage in networking and pitch to donors, proactively lead on funding applications , develop new ideas for fundraising, ensure submitted proposals are of high quality and support the various teams with their thematic fundraising as we operate with a decentralised approach . The development side of the job entails keeping our donor- and project database up to date, organising trainings for staff , researching funding opportunities and engaging the membership in our fundraising efforts to generate win-win opportunities. This role offers room to grow, professionally and personally. You will have opportunities to deepen your expertise, take on new responsibilities, and help further strengthen a strategic approach to donor stewardship in a hands-on fundraising role at a large, European network. You will work closely with and report to the Director of Membership and Governance, support the internal Senior Management and Fundraising Team, and coordinate and support the fundraising efforts across the different EEB teams. What You Will Actually Do Implementation of the 2025 – 2030 EEB fundraising strategy: Supporting the Senior Management Team and internal Fundraising Team with strategic fundraising, donor relations and meetings; Monitoring the implementation of the EEB fundraising strategy and annual action plans and capture learnings. Research and proactive fundraising in line with agreed priorities: Researching funding opportunities and supporting the various EEB teams with their thematic fundraising in line with our decentralised approach; Coordinating the EEB application and reports for the EU LIFE Programme operating grant. Developing and submitting own project proposals. Donor, Member and Partner Relations: Coordinating the EEB’s donor outreach to avoid overlap; Supporting and presenting at meetings of various EEB initiatives, donor groups and membership fundraising task forces; Encouraging joint fundraising with EEB members and partners. Managing the EEB project database and donor tracker: Keeping the EEB project database and donor tracker up to date; Organising regular check-ins with team leads to ensure that data related to fundraising efforts is up to date. MEL Frameworks and training: Proposing ideas for improvement or change in all operational areas; Keeping the EEB Project Management Guide and other fundraising support material up to date; Organising regular staff trainings on fundraising and project management. Who You Are As the EEB’s next Fundraising and Development Officer, you will typically have 2-3+ years of relevant experience in fundraising, proven direct fundraising experience with some successful project applications on your CV, an entrepreneurial mindset and a personal commitment to the work we do. Your Skills & Experiences: 2-3+ years of experience in fundraising and development with an initial track record of submitted and successful applications; Good knowledge of the funding landscape for Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) operating at European level; Experience of direct fundraising as well as having supported others in their fundraising work (research on suitable donors, application writing, quality controls, budgeting, project implementation from A to Z); Good knowledge of healthy project management principles and suitable Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning frameworks for CSOs; Strong command of written and spoken English; Good communication and presentation skills (Powerpoints etc.); CRM and contact database management skills; Enjoys coordination, keeping overviews, supporting colleagues and helping the organisation to stick to agreed timelines and deadlines; Solid planning skills, highly motivated, creative, proactive, friendly and diplomatic (mastering the art of the gentle reminder). Assets That Make You Stand Out: Experience in having worked for a civil society, membership or other purpose-driven organisation is a strong asset; Knowledge of the Salesforce environment is an asset (training will be provided); Working knowledge of French with any other language skills being appreciated. Your Values: You care about the environment and subscribe to the EEB’s values . Why You Will Love Working With Us A full-time, permanent contract (80% role negotiable if preferred); An organisation committed to its values of democracy, fairness, respect, integrity and sustainability, and a purpose-driven, supportive and friendly team with 70+ people working for a better future in which people and nature thrive together; An attractive workspace in the heart of the EU quarter and a healthy organisational culture , including, for instance, staff away days and (optional) social gatherings; Possibility to work from home 4 days a week and from another EU country for up to six weeks per year; Flexible working hours with a transparent floating time system ; A monthly gross salary starting from EUR 3101, with a higher salary depending on the level of experience. Please check our salary scale ; Various monetary benefits , including a holiday bonus, 13 th month, a generous pension scheme, lunch vouchers, teleworking indemnity, transport allowance, travel insurance, and phone subscription [not for temporary contracts]; Quality trainings (group and individual), peer learning and skills shares; Next to 20 days of legal leave, we offer 5 days of extra-legal leave during the winter break closure, 5 days of extra-legal leave anytime in the year and 2 days of extra-legal leave days for office-wide long weekends in spring and autumn, that is, a total of 32 paid leave days, plus seniority leave (up to 10 extra days), and paid leave for compelling reasons. Registration in Belgium and work permits As our contracts fall under Belgian law, the candidate must commit to being officially registered in Belgium and working from our office in Brussels (with structural teleworking). The EEB welcomes applicants from outside the EU , and we consider it a privilege to have non-EU nationals amongst our staff members and to benefit from their perspectives and skills. If you are not an EU citizen, please let us know if you have a work permit for Belgium . Please note that it is not always possible for us to initiate and succeed with work permit applications for non-EU nationals due to legal restrictions, additional costs and practical issues for a medium-sized non-profit organisation. If you do not hold a work permit for Belgium, please feel free to reach out to request further information before you apply. If you hold a work permit, please mention if you hold a valid Single Permit (A card) or permanent residence permit (B card, long-term resident). How You Can Apply We are looking forward to receiving: a short letter of motivation ; your CV (without pictures); a completed questionnaire (see below). We value clarity, motivation and authenticity more than formal letters and too much detail. Only applications comprising these three elements will be considered. item.description: Legal & Data Protection Officer Eurofound - The European Foundation for the Improvement of Living & Working Conditions Dublin, Ireland JOB CONTEXT & DUTIES The Organisational Support Unit provides a range of services for the efficient development and implementation of Eurofound’s operations through various planning and management information systems, workflows and management and performance reporting tools. The Unit is also responsible for supporting the Executive Director and staff in areas of legal advice, data protection, document management and internal control. The duties will require to work on a variety of organisation-wide tasks in good collaboration with colleagues in the Unit as well as with colleagues across the organisation. The Legal & Data Protection Officer will be based in the Organisational Support Unit and will contribute to the achievement of Eurofound’s objectives by providing legal advice and support on the interpretation and application of the legal framework governing Eurofound’s operational and administrative activities. The successful candidate will also be appointed as the Data Protection Officer overseeing Eurofound’s data protection strategy and implementation in accordance with the applicable Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. The duties of the post include: Legal advice and consultation: Providing input in respect of all legal aspects relevant to the functioning of Eurofound, including on matters related to staff and financial regulations, governance structure, data protection, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and contractual matters including intellectual property rights. Drafting legal opinions and documents on the application and interpretation of Eurofound’s legal framework as well as any other applicable legal provisions of Union law. Drafting decisions of the Management Board or other bodies of Eurofound’s governance structure. Contributing to the preparation and implementation of arrangements with other Union institutions and bodies, and other external partners. Cooperating with external legal advisors; including those that may represent the Agency in litigation before the Court of Justice of the European Union. Data Protection: Informing and advising staff on their obligations pursuant to the Data Protection Regulation. Preparing and monitoring policies and guidelines on data protection. Conducting regular assessments. Maintaining records of all data processing activities Serving as the point of contact between the Agency and the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS). General: Collaborating with staff in achieving compliance with the legal framework and awareness of data protection requirements in the agency’s operations. Providing training and coaching in regulatory compliance – in collaboration with staff in HR, Internal control and ICT (on AI and cybersecurity). Representing Eurofound in inter-agency networks on legal matters and data protection. Other tasks assigned by the Head of Unit. item.description: Executive Director GFI Europe - Good Food Institute Europe Remote, UK or Belgium €109,925 - €123.907 or £90,500 - £104,000 The Good Food Institute Europe (GFI Europe) is a nonprofit think tank at the forefront of the movement to transform meat production in order to solve some of the world’s biggest problems, from climate change and global hunger to antibiotic resistance and animal suffering. Our vision is a thriving world, fed sustainably. With a nonprofit entity in Belgium, a branch in the UK and colleagues working from seven other countries that make up GFI Europe, we are also part of an international network of affiliates. We advance the science, policies and investment needed to make plant-based, cultivated and fermentation-made meat delicious, affordable and accessible across Europe. Please check out the rest of our website , our 2025 Year in Review and our 2025 Europe highlights blog post to find out more about who we are and what we do. We are looking for an Executive Director to lead GFI Europe’s strategy and team, play a key role in shaping and advancing GFI’s global strategy, and foster the relationships and organisational strength needed to accelerate the shift towards a resilient and sustainable food system. How you will make a difference: You will have high responsibility and high impact. Reporting to, and appointed by, the Board of GFI Europe, you will lead a ~50-person team working from nine European countries. You will: Enable strategic focus: Align the team around a clear and compelling organisational direction that aligns with the GFI network’s mission and theory of change; Translate organisational direction into high-level priorities in collaboration with GFI Europe’s Leadership Team; Ensure Europe’s strategic decisions are made well – soliciting the right input from the right people, preserving autonomy in areas of specific expertise, and making decisions when organisation-wide trade-offs are required; Take ultimate responsibility for maximising outcomes and impact in pursuit of our mission. Provide leadership to the team: Empower, develop and inspire a high-performing, people-centric team; Lead GFI Europe’s Leadership Team, formed of six department heads, ensuring they continue to function on a ‘first-team’ basis to achieve organisational objectives; Champion and uphold a values-driven culture built upon transparency, autonomy, collaboration, accountability, and psychological safety. Champion the integration of diversity, equity and inclusion into the team’s day-to-day work. Represent GFI Europe in GFI’s international network: Participate in international strategic and coordination workstreams as a member of GFI’s Regional Leadership Group, comprising GFI’s affiliate leads; Act as the primary liaison between GFI’s affiliates and European teams on strategies, processes and goals. Ensure the Europe team can successfully connect with, influence, support and navigate a complex international network, including global workstreams such as fundraising and impact reporting; Participate in discussions about global strategy and resource allocation so as to maximise GFI’s overall mission impact, including communicating GFI Europe’s strategy, resourcing needs and contributions as part of the international GFI network. Represent GFI Europe in front of donors and external stakeholders: Work closely with global and Europe-based fundraising teams to help ensure GFI achieves its fundraising goals; Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, prospective supporters and key stakeholders; Serve as a public representative of, and spokesperson for, the organisation by speaking at conferences, events, and with the media. Oversee organisational health: Ensure strong governance, legal compliance, financial sustainability and reporting in partnership with the Board and the Head of Operations; Be the main legal representative of the organisation, reviewing and signing all legally relevant agreements and organisational documents. Perform other duties as appropriate. Core capabilities needed to succeed in this role: Mission alignment. A passion for GFI’s philosophy and mission . Strategic judgement. Strong analytical skills and sound judgement, being able to absorb and process a range of types of information, understand the activities that GFI undertakes, and provide leadership and guidance to team members. You have the experience and ability to make strategic trade-offs across projects, functions, teams, countries/regions, programmes, etc. – weighing resource allocation, prioritising impact, and communicating those decisions clearly and inclusively to stakeholders; Thoughtful leadership. You align teams behind a clear and impactful vision. You know when to persevere and when to change course, and have led people, both directly and indirectly, to deliver impact. You trust the people closest to the work to make decisions, and you address hard topics when they truly matter. You own mistakes and make a genuine effort to learn and grow from them. You are intentional about remote leadership; Understanding the wider context. You can make sense of the political, economic and cultural forces shaping Europe’s food system today and are adept at drawing on patterns and ideas from outside our field to identify possible implications for GFI Europe’s next move; Excellent people skills. High emotional intelligence and an ability to diplomatically engage across perspectives, being able to build and maintain trust with colleagues and stakeholders across multiple cultures, viewpoints and needs within Europe and beyond; Financial literacy. Skilled at overseeing substantial financial resources, including partnering with the operations team on resource allocation. You have held accountability for a significant organisational budget and can interpret financial data to make sound, well-informed decisions; Fundraising acumen. You understand how GFI’s strategy, culture, and mission impact shape the organisation’s ability to raise funds and steward donors, and you’re enthusiastic about partnering with the fundraising team to make this happen. You bring an understanding of the philanthropic sector and donor relationships, or of fundraising in other sectors (eg, the private sector or government), while deferring to the fundraising team’s expertise on how donor relationships are best managed; Strong communication skills. An ability to convincingly articulate and explain our mission and work and to represent the organisation in the media, with programmatic stakeholders, and with donors. Comfort adapting your tone and message for different audiences across diverse cultures, and excellent verbal and written English skills; Flexible approach to work. We estimate that travel will account for approximately six weeks of the year. This will likely consist of two GFI Europe team-wide retreats (3-5 days each), one leadership retreat (2-3 days), other sporadic trips generally lasting 1-3 days, and occasional longer trips of approximately 5-7 days (for conferences and donor or partner meetings across Europe and internationally). In addition, you will need occasional flexibility in your working hours to accommodate coordination with other affiliates around the world; Integrity. You do what you say you’ll do, and are discreet when handling confidential information. It would be an advantage to have the following, though none are prerequisites: Sector familiarity. Familiarity with or experience working in the food system, alternative proteins or an adjacent sector in Europe; Impact leadership. Strong knowledge and/or experience of being part of the leadership team of a nonprofit, think tank or other social impact-focused organisation; Governance and compliance experience. Experience with legal representation and board reporting, and/or experience working on nonprofit compliance, especially in Belgium; Fundraising partnership experience. You’ve contributed to fundraising in a supportive capacity – whether managing a fundraising function, advising on donor and prospect strategy, joining donor conversations alongside a development team, or shaping fundraising strategy at an executive level; Network experience. Experience working in one or more network models (eg, affiliate or franchise-style, federation, confederation, etc.); Languages. The ability to work in European languages in addition to English. The Fine Print: Terms of employment: Full-time (flexible hours), permanent; Location: This role can be based in either Belgium or the United Kingdom, where GFI Europe has established entities and where you must have the right to work. We actively encourage applications from people across Europe, and a relocation package is available for candidates moving to either country if necessary: Relocation support will be provided with a budget of up to £8,000 in the UK or €8,700 in Belgium, which can be used for transport, temporary housing, and other relocation expenses deemed necessary. Salary and benefits: The salary and benefits packages for all of our roles are researched and benchmarked based on similar nonprofit roles in the country/location of hire. Belgium: €7,900-€8,900 gross monthly salary (€109,925-€123.907 annually, including 13 th month and holiday pay). Plus benefits including home-working allowance (if applicable), meal vouchers, eco vouchers, and professional development allocation; United Kingdom: £90,500-£104,000 gross annual salary. You can read more about our wider benefits offering here ; Right to work requirements: The successful candidate must, by the start of the employment, have permission to work in the country where they are based for the role, and be able to travel within the EU and internationally; Application Deadline: 13 September 2026, 11.59pm CEST. item.description: Lead Advisor Navigate Brussels, Belgium Are you motivated by advising defence-industry leaders on European policy, institutional engagement, partnerships, and funding? Do you combine sound political judgement with a commercial mindset, and enjoy taking responsibility for client relationships, complex assignments, and the development of colleagues and business? Then you might be our new Lead Advisor. We are looking for an experienced, trusted, and proactive colleague who will work with our teams in Brussels and Copenhagen to deliver strategic advice to clients and help further develop our Brussels office and European defence practice. Who we are Navigate is a growing strategic advisory firm specializing in the defence and security sector. From our offices in Copenhagen and Brussels, we help companies understand political decision-making, identify business opportunities and engage effectively with public authorities and institutions. We opened our Brussels office in January 2026 to support companies operating in Europe’s rapidly devel-oping defence landscape. Led by our Head of Office, the Brussels operation has gained strong momentum, and we are now expanding the team. As a senior member of the team, you will have the opportunity to take significant responsibility for client relationships and assignments and contribute to the continued de-velopment of our Brussels office and European defence practice. Our Brussels team advises clients on EU and NATO affairs, European defence programmes and national defence markets. Our work spans policy intelligence and opportunity identification, strategic advocacy and stakeholder engagement, as well as guidance on European funding programmes, consortium building and proposals. Navigate combines the specialist expertise and close collaboration of a focused advisory firm with an inter-national outlook and ambitious plans for growth. We provide clear, fact-based and trusted advice, and our senior advisors play an important role in maintaining the quality of our work, developing long-term client relationships and identifying new opportunities for our clients and our business. Just as importantly, Navigate is a place where you can be yourself. Our culture is built on integrity, inclusiveness, expertise and mutual respect. We share knowledge, speak candidly and support one another in delivering exceptional results for our clients. What will you be working on? As Lead Advisor, you will take ownership of client relationships and assignments across our reporting, advocacy, and grants work. You will collaborate closely with colleagues in Brussels and Copenhagen, combine strategic judgement with hands-on delivery, and help grow Navigate's Brussels office and European defence practice. Your tasks will include: Leading client accounts and workstreams, from scoping and strategic advice to delivery, quality control, budgets, and client satisfaction; Turning clients' technologies and commercial priorities into policy, engagement, partnership, and funding strategies; Providing political and programme intelligence, identifying opportunities and risks, and producing clear recommendations for senior decision-makers; Designing and implementing advocacy strategies and facilitating dialogue with EU institutions, NATO stakeholders, national delegations, Ministries of Defence, industry, and potential partners; Guiding grant and tender work, including award-criteria analysis, narrative development, consortium formation, partner coordination, and proposal quality assurance; Developing business opportunities, contributing to pitches, strengthening Navigate's network, and mentoring junior colleagues while remaining ready to handle practical delivery tasks. Who are you? We imagine that you have at least seven years of relevant professional experience, including substantial work in or with the Brussels EU and/or NATO defence and security environment. Exceptional candidates with slightly less experience and unusually strong client, network, and delivery credentials will also be considered. What matters most is that you: Have deep knowledge of European defence policy and industry and strong policy awareness: you understand the interaction between the EU, NATO, national governments, Ministries of Defence, and companies, and anticipate how political priorities may affect clients; Bring an active, trusted network across relevant institutions, national representations, defence organisations, industry associations, and companies - and use relationships ethically and with discretion; Combine commercial awareness with political and institutional expertise: you understand client technologies, market positions, and strategic priorities and translate complex issues into clear recommendations; Demonstrate excellent political judgement, integrity, confidentiality, and the confidence to give candid advice when a proposed course of action is unsuitable; Have experience leading client accounts or major workstreams and consistently delivering high-quality work across complex assignments and competing priorities; Can develop business, shape compelling offers, and build long-term client relationships and at the same time keep high delivery standards; Are a versatile team player who mentors colleagues, shares credit, and remains willing to move from strategy to detailed execution; Communicate and write to an excellent professional standard in English. Direct experience in an EU institution, NATO, a national Ministry of Defence, a Permanent Representation, the defence industry, or a specialist consultancy is a strong advantage. Experience in at least two of the three Navigate service areas - reporting, advocacy, and grants - is preferred, together with credible working knowledge of the third. Additional European languages and experience with procurement, export controls, or capability development are welcome. The role is based at our office in Brussels' EU district and involves occasional travel within Europe, including to our Copenhagen office. You must be eligible to work in Belgium. The indicative starting date is 1 November 2026. A role with influence At Navigate, you will advise clients on complex issues at the intersection of European defence, politics and business. Your advice will help senior decision-makers understand political developments, engage effectively with key stakeholders and identify strategic opportunities across the European defence landscape. You will take a leading role in client relationships and assignments, working closely with colleagues in Brussels and Copenhagen. You will have the opportunity to shape strategic advice, develop services and client relationships, mentor colleagues and contribute to the continued development of our Brussels office and European defence practice. We offer a high degree of responsibility and freedom, strong professional standards and a collaborative, cross-European working environment. You will receive onboarding in both Brussels and Copenhagen, role-specific training and the opportunity to influence the development of Navigate as our company and Brussels office continue to grow. Our flat hierarchy gives you direct access to Navigate’s leadership and the freedom to act on sound judgement and new ideas. You will be trusted to take ownership, provide candid advice and make a visible contribution to our clients, colleagues and business. Interested? If this sounds like you, please upload your CV and a motivated application in English through our recruitment system. We review applications on a rolling basis. Please apply no later than 15 September 2026 . We expect to hold first-round interviews on 22-23 September and second-round interviews on 28-29 September. We therefore encourage you to reserve these dates when applying. Apply Now Deadline 15 September Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying. Share this Job

item.description: HR Policy and Employee Relations Advisor (Re-issued Vacancy - Previous Candidates Need Not Reapply) ESO - European Southern Observatory Garching, Germany The European Organisation for Astronomical Research in the Southern Hemisphere (ESO) is the foremost intergovernmental astronomy organisation in Europe and the world's most productive ground-based astronomical observatory. ESO carries out an ambitious programme focused on the design, construction and operation of powerful ground-based observing facilities enabling astronomers to make important scientific discoveries. ESO operates three unique world-class observing sites in northern Chile: La Silla, Paranal and Chajnantor (home to ALMA), and the ESO Headquarters are located in Garching, near Munich, Germany. At Paranal, ESO operates the Very Large Telescope, the world's most advanced visible-light astronomical observatory, and will host and operate the southern array of the Cherenkov Telescope Array, the world's largest and most sensitive high energy gamma-ray observatory. ESO is a major partner in ALMA. On Cerro Armazones, ESO is building the 39-metre Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which will become "the world's biggest eye on the sky" and whose operations will be fully integrated into the Paranal Observatory. It is against this backdrop of scientific ambition and organisational growth that ESO is launching its People Strategy 2026 to 2031, a five-year programme designed to future-proof its workforce and ensure ESO can attract, develop and retain the people it needs for the decade ahead. Human Resources sits at the centre of that effort, combining high-quality day-to-day service to staff and management with an active role in helping to shape the organisation for the future. Joining an HR department that operates as ''HR One'' between Germany and Chile, and arising from an internal reorganisation pending the launch of the ESO People Strategy in late 2026, we are seeking to hire a: HR Policy and Employee Relations Advisor. ESO is building the world's biggest eye on the sky. This role helps build the people strategy behind it. This is a genuinely blended role. ESO is looking for a person who can move between HR policy development and employee relations casework, not a policy specialist or an employee relations specialist alone. Candidates should be drawn to both areas in their HR career journey and have demonstrable, hands-on experience. Human Resources plays a central role in supporting ESO's strategic objectives by providing a comprehensive, high-quality service to staff and management. This position is a great opportunity for an experienced HR professional to influence how policy and employee relations are practiced across a scientific organisation entering a period of significant change. Rather than administering an established framework, the successful candidate will help design one, working at the intersection of day-to-day HR advice, policy development in the framework of the recently established People Strategy, and some of the most consequential governance conversations happening inside ESO today. You will work closely with managers, staff representatives and other HR colleagues, and you will be line manager of an HR Policy Officer, giving you scope to build not just policy, but a team. Main Duties and Responsibilities You will: Manage and drive the development, review and implementation of HR policies and frameworks, ensuring alignment with organisational needs and best practices; Collaborate with staff representation bodies, supporting constructive social dialogue and follow-up actions; Provide expert HR advice and guidance to managers and staff on policies, procedures and employment conditions; Actively support and, where appropriate, lead HR projects and strategic initiatives, such as: Organisational Development; reviews of Staff Regulations and internal policies; benchmarking of employment conditions; Prepare HR proposals, reports and presentations for internal governance bodies and senior management; Conduct research and analysis on HR trends and best practices to inform decision-making; Represent HR in internal working groups and committees; Contribute to the continuous improvement of HR processes, systems and services. The role requires flexibility and the ability to operate across a broad range of HR topics in an evolving organisational context. Reports to Programme Manager - People Strategy (a role which also acts as HR Policy and Employee Relations Team Leader). This reporting line reflects the central role that HR policy and employee relations expertise plays in delivering significant strategic objectives under the People Strategy. The postholder will be fully integrated into the broader HR function in the HR Business partnering group under the overall leadership of the Head of Human Resources. Key competences and experience Essential: A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in Human Resources is required, ideally in an international or complex multi-national organisational environment; Proven experience in developing, reviewing and implementing HR policies; Experience in Employee Relations management, including advising on and managing individual employee cases, interpreting HR policies and employment frameworks, and engaging with staff associations/unions or other staff representative bodies; Strong knowledge of employment frameworks, policies and HR practices (experience with staff regulations or similar frameworks is an asset); Ability to balance operational delivery with strategic thinking; Confidence to challenge and improve existing practices; Analytical mindset with attention to detail; Ability to manage multiple priorities and work under time constraints; Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence and build trust; Collaborative approach, with the ability to work both independently and as part of a team. Desirable: Project management in a leadership capacity; Change management experience; Familiarity with HR in international organisations; Familiarity with HR information systems; Supervisory skills. item.description: Sector Officer - Civil Society - VA 28/2026 FMO - Financial Mechanism Office Brussels, Belgium From € 117,072 per year Are you a dynamic, motivated professional looking to make a positive impact in Europe? We are looking for a new Sector Officer-Civil Society, to join the Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) in Brussels. About Us: The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) - affiliated with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) - is the international secretariat carrying out the day-to-day management of the EEA and Norway Grants. The Grants are Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway’s contribution to reducing economic and social disparities in the European Economic Area (EEA) and strengthen bilateral relations and partnerships between the Donor States and the 15 Beneficiary States (Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia). The EEA Grants are financed by the three donor countries whereas Norway Grants are financed solely by Norway. The current funding period has a total budget of 3.2 billion euros. The programmes in this funding period will focus on these overall priorities: European green transition; Democracy, rule of law and human rights; Social inclusion and resilience. Why join the FMO? We offer more than just a job. We offer a stimulating and diverse international workplace with a trust-based culture. Our team of more than 60 employees from the EEA region brings a rich blend of experiences and knowledge to our daily operations. We are committed to fostering a collaborative and respectful environment where you can advance your career. Every day, our work is driven by a shared goal: a green, democratic and resilient Europe where everyone can take meaningful part in shaping their lives. We work closely with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of the Donor States (Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway), the 15 Beneficiary States and various international partners. Learn more: If you are ready to take on a rewarding challenge and be part of a dedicated team working towards improving economic and social equality and strengthening cooperation and partnerships in Europe, we encourage you to apply. For more details about our work and the opportunities we offer, please visit our website at www.eeagrants.org . The position is open to nationals of EEA EFTA States (Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway). Division: Financial Mechanism Office Category/Level: A4 This is a fixed-term contract for three years. The contract is renewable once, subject to the renewal being in the interest of the FMO and to a decision on the new funding period following the current Financial Mechanisms. Start Date: As soon as possible Closing Date: 23-09-2026 Job Reference: VA 27/2026 Scope: The Civil Society Fund supports an independent, vibrant, and resilient civil society as a cornerstone of democracy, rule of law and human rights, representing 10% of the total allocation of the EEA and Norway Grants. Through grant-making, capacity building, advocacy and civic participation initiatives, the Civil Society Fund contributes to strengthening civic space, promoting citizen engagement, supporting groups marginalised by society, and enhancing the capacity and sustainability of civil society organisations. For the Financial Mechanisms 2021-2028, the Civil Society Fund is managed by the Donor States, and the FMO acts as Programme Operator. Each of the national allocations of the Civil Society Fund are implemented by independent Fund Operators (a consortium of civil society organisations) selected through open calls. You will manage a portfolio of Civil Society Fund programmes in selected Beneficiary States, supporting their development and implementation and serving as the primary point of contact for the Fund Operators in these countries. As programme manager, you will lead interdisciplinary programme teams within the FMO, working closely with colleagues responsible for legal, financial, results, communication and country-related matters. You will also contribute to the FMO’s strategic and policy-related work on civil society, including engagement with European and international stakeholders, monitoring developments affecting civil society across Europe, and supporting the implementation of donor priorities related to democracy, rule of law, civic participation, civic space and human rights. In addition, you will manage the Fund for Social Dialogue and Decent Work. This Fund is one of the instruments of the Norway Grants and supports stronger cooperation between employers, employees and public authorities to promote decent work, inclusive labour markets, gender equality, lifelong learning and fair working conditions, contributing to social inclusion and resilient societies. Key responsibilities will include contributing to the development and implementation of the Fund and acting as the primary contact point for the independent Fund Operator, with the support of a dedicated interdisciplinary team within the FMO. You may be required to work in other areas, according to the needs and priorities of the FMO. The position involves travel. You will report to the Head of the Funds and Horizontal Concerns Unit. Responsibilities and tasks: As a Sector Officer for Civil Society and programme manager for a selection of Civil Society Fund programmes, your role will generally include: Programme management: Oversee and manage a portfolio of Civil Society Fund programmes in the Beneficiary States, supporting their development and implementation and leading and coordinating programme teams within the FMO; Primary liaison with Fund Operators: Maintain regular communication with relevant Fund Operators and other programme stakeholders, ensuring effective cooperation and timely resolution of any issues; Communication of priorities and results: Compile, analyse and communicate programme results, lessons learned and emerging trends; Monitoring developments affecting civil society: Monitor trends, challenges and opportunities related to civil society, civic space, citizen participation, democracy, rule of law and human rights across Europe and provide strategic advice to the Donor States; Policy development and stakeholder engagement: Contribute to policy discussions and initiatives related to civil society at European level, including engagement with EU institutions, international organisations, donor state actors, bilateral relations and civil society networks; Supporting strategic cooperation and partnerships: Promote cooperation between civil society organisations, Donor State entities and international partners; Engaging with Donors: Contribute to dialogue with Donors on programme development, implementation, results and strategic priorities related to civil society. As a Sector Officer in charge of the Fund for Social Dialogue and Decent Work, your role will include: Monitoring Fund implementation, results, budgets, and reporting; Acting as the main liaison with the Fund Operator, social partners, and donor stakeholders; Supporting governance meetings and stakeholder engagement; Contributing to risk management, compliance, evaluations, and visibility activities; Facilitating knowledge-sharing and the exchange of good practices across beneficiary states. Qualifications: A Master’s-level university degree in a relevant field. Experience and skills: Essential experience and skills: A minimum of six years of relevant professional experience, including a minimum of five years of experience in grant, programme and/or project management; Demonstrated experience in working with organisations responsible for the implementation of programmes, including oversight, monitoring and capacity building; Proven experience with grant, programme and/or project management, such as monitoring progress, assessing risks, ensuring results-based management and preparing reports; Demonstrated knowledge of European policies, initiatives and developments relevant to the civil society sector; Demonstrated strong interpersonal skills with cultural sensitivity and a flexible, pragmatic and result-oriented attitude, including the ability to identify operational challenges and propose actionable solutions; Strong organisational skills with an ability to work proactively and manage parallel processes and deadlines; Knowledge of the Nordic tripartite cooperation model (employers, employees and public authorities). Desirable experience and skills: Strong strategic and analytical skills, including ability to work across programmes or projects to communicate results; Knowledge of the Donors States’ and/or Beneficiary States’ policies and priorities in civil society; Knowledge of governance models and multi-stakeholder engagement approaches in the Donor States, including cooperation between public authorities, social partners and civil society organisations; Understanding of the EEA and Norway Grants framework. A great work environment and strong teamwork define the FMO, and we look for candidates who actively contribute to both. item.title: (Senior) Adviseur Public Affairs Europa
item.description: (Senior) Adviseur Public Affairs Europa Provincie Utrecht Brussels, Belgium €5,118.26 - €7,233.84 per month gross Zorg dat de belangen van de provincie Utrecht een sterke plek krijgen in Europa. Vanuit Brussel verbind je Europese ontwikkelingen met de opgaven van Utrecht en help je het provinciebestuur om invloed uit te oefenen op besluiten die onze provincie raken. Wat ga je doen Je werkt vanuit het Huis van de Nederlandse Provincies (HNP) in Brussel. Samen met collega’s van andere provincies volg je Europese ontwikkelingen en bepaal je welke ontwikkelingen belangrijk zijn voor Utrecht. Je brengt deze informatie actief onder de aandacht van collega’s en bestuurders en zorgt dat Utrecht op het juiste moment aan tafel zit. Je vertegenwoordigt de provincie bij Europese instellingen, Brusselse organisaties en relevante bijeenkomsten. Je onderhoudt een breed netwerk en gebruikt dit netwerk om informatie op te halen, contacten te leggen en Utrecht zichtbaar te maken. Ook organiseer je werkbezoeken en evenementen waarmee je bestuurders en collega’s in contact brengt met Europese partners. Binnen de provincie werk je nauw samen met het Utrechtse Europateam, inhoudelijke afdelingen, management, directie en het college van Gedeputeerde Staten. Je adviseert over Europese dossiers en helpt bestuurders om hun rol in Brussel goed te vervullen. Ook draag je bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van de Europese samenwerking van de provincie. Verder ga je: Europese ontwikkelingen vertalen naar duidelijke signalen en adviezen voor Utrecht; Utrechtse belangen inbrengen in het Europese besluitvormingsproces; De bestuurlijk portefeuillehouder Europa adviseren en ondersteunen in Brussel, het Huis van de Nederlandse Provincies, het Comité van de Regio’s en in Randstadverband; Europese kennis en ontwikkelingen delen met collega’s binnen de provincie; Regionale samenwerking met gemeenten, andere overheden en maatschappelijke partners versterken. Wat bieden wij? Werken bij de provincie Utrecht betekent dat je een waardevolle bijdrage levert aan het oplossen van maatschappelijke opgaven. Deze opgaven vragen het bijeenbrengen van veel verschillende disciplines en belangen – vooral buiten, maar ook binnen de organisatie. Als medewerker vorm jij de verbindende schakel. We halen kennis op, delen onze deskundigheid en behalen met elkaar successen. Samen komen we verder. We investeren in de ontwikkeling van onze medewerkers. Je krijgt volop de gelegenheid voor eigen initiatief en ruimte om te groeien. Wij vinden een gezonde balans tussen werk en privé belangrijk. Iedereen krijgt de kans om flexibel en naar eigen vermogen te werken. Bij de provincie Utrecht werken we hybride. Hoe dit eruit ziet geven we samen vorm. De organisatie is in ontwikkeling. We maken een professionaliseringsslag en gaan steeds meer opgavegericht werken. Als jij het leuk vindt om het voortouw te nemen en verder mee wilt bouwen aan onze organisatie, garanderen wij jou een boeiende tijd. Naast uitdagend werk en leuke collega’s bieden we jou: Een tijdelijke arbeidsovereenkomst van één jaar voor 32 tot 36 uur per week met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband; Een salaris tussen de € 5.118,26 en € 7.233,84 bruto per maand op basis van een fulltime dienstverband van 36 uur per week (schaalniveau 12). Afhankelijk van kennis en ervaring start je in een aanloopschaal 11; Een Individueel Keuze Budget van 22,37% boven op je maandelijkse salaris dat je onder andere kan inzetten voor extra vrije tijd, studie of meer salaris; Een persoonlijk budget voor duurzame inzetbaarheid van € 6.000,- per 5 jaar. Ook kun je gebruik maken van ons interne trainingsaanbod van de UtrechtAcademie; Een goede pensioenregeling bij het ABP; Als je bij ons fulltime werkt, heb je een werkweek van 36 uur en heb je recht op 18 vakantiedagen. Je mag ook meer uur werken, je bouwt dan extra compensatieverlof op. Zo kan je bij een fulltime dienstverband tot wel 25,5 extra vakantiedagen opbouwen! Kijk voor meer informatie over uren en verlof op onze arbeidsvoorwaardenpagina . Wie zoeken wij? Je bent nieuwsgierig naar wat er in Europa gebeurt en begrijpt hoe Europese besluitvorming werkt. Je kunt snel hoofd- en bijzaken onderscheiden en weet welke ontwikkelingen voor Utrecht van belang zijn. Je combineert strategisch inzicht met een praktische aanpak: je ziet wat er moet gebeuren en komt vervolgens in actie. Je bent sterk in het onderhouden van contacten en het opbouwen van netwerken. In Brussel werk je met verschillende organisaties en belangen. Je kunt daarin goed bewegen, legt makkelijk verbindingen en weet anderen mee te krijgen. Ook wanneer belangen uiteenlopen, blijf je gericht op een concreet resultaat. Je schrijft helder en overtuigend. Je kunt complexe Europese ontwikkelingen vertalen naar een kort advies, een position paper, lobbyfiche, spreektekst of stemadvies. Daarnaast ben je flexibel en stressbestendig. Je kunt snel schakelen tussen verschillende onderwerpen en werkzaamheden, bijvoorbeeld tussen een overleg bij een Europese instelling en de voorbereiding van een werkbezoek voor een bestuurder. Verder beschik je als adviseur Public Affairs Europa over: Hbo- of wo-werk- en -denkniveau, bij voorkeur in politicologie, Europese studies, bestuurskunde, rechten of een vergelijkbare richting; Minimaal 3 jaar aantoonbare werkervaring in Europese Public Affairs, bijvoorbeeld bij een decentrale overheid, branchevereniging of Public Affairs-kantoor; Uitstekende mondelinge en schriftelijke vaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels; Ervaring met het schrijven van ambtelijke en bestuurlijke adviezen, annotaties en rapportages in een politiek-bestuurlijke omgeving; Kennis van de Europese instellingen en Europese wet- en regelgeving en de manier waarop Europese besluitvorming tot stand komt. Wie zijn wij? Utrecht is een provincie om trots op te zijn. Gevarieerd, bruisend en met een rijke historie. Met veel verschillende levensstijlen, culturen en persoonlijke voorkeuren. Onze regio is een topregio met een innovatieve kenniseconomie. Het is onze opgave om de aantrekkelijkheid van onze provincie te vergroten en groei zo te faciliteren dat de kwaliteit van onze ruimte behouden blijft. Samen met inwoners, bedrijven, organisaties en andere overheden werken het provinciebestuur en medewerkers met enthousiasme en daadkracht aan een gezonde en duurzame leefomgeving. Wij willen dat iedereen in de provincie Utrecht fantastisch woont, werkt en leeft. Daarom zorgen wij voor een goede balans tussen groen en groei. Je komt te werken bij het domein Strategie & Bestuur van de provincie Utrecht. Dit domein ondersteunt bestuur en directie bij het realiseren van de doelen van de provincie. Daarbij werken collega’s vanuit verschillende vakgebieden samen en zoeken zij actief de verbinding met partners buiten de organisatie. Binnen Strategie & Bestuur valt het team Strategie, Europa en Public Affairs (SEP). Het team werkt aan verschillende onderwerpen, zoals strategie en kennis, Europese zaken, Public Affairs in Den Haag en Utrecht Advies. De sfeer is open en ontspannen. Collega’s geven elkaar ruimte en helpen elkaar om het werk steeds beter te doen. Kritische feedback hoort daarbij. Je maakt onderdeel uit van het cluster Europa. Dit cluster vormt de verbinding tussen de Europese instellingen en de provincie Utrecht. Het cluster houdt zich bezig met Europese belangenbehartiging, het benutten van Europese subsidiemogelijkheden, internationale profilering en het vergroten van Europese kennis binnen de organisatie en de regio. Je werkt vanuit het Huis van de Nederlandse Provincies in Brussel. Daar werk je samen met vertegenwoordigers van andere Nederlandse provincies. Tegelijkertijd houd je nauw contact met collega’s in Utrecht. Zo ben je onderdeel van zowel de Brusselse als de Utrechtse organisatie. Solliciteren Ben je geïnteresseerd?
